heading: INT. CLOSED ICE-CREAM PARLOR - BACK ROOM - NIGHT

units.text: INT. CLOSED ICE-CREAM PARLOR - BACK ROOM - NIGHT
Pastel walls and a dead freezer.
A single bulb.
VINCENT "VINNIE" DELACORTE (50s, suit, tie loosened) sits at a small table.
Across from him, DETECTIVE MARGARET "MAGS" OYELARAN (40s, gray blazer) turns a sundae spoon over in her fingers.
You came alone.
units.name: VINNIE

units.text: I did.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: Somebody always comes alone.
units.name: VINNIE

units.text: He pours himself coffee from a thermos and slides a second cup across.
She does not touch it.
He drinks.
The silence stretches.
You know what I miss? The chocolate chip.
units.name: VINNIE

units.text: Is that right.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: My mother worked here. Thirty years behind that counter.
units.name: VINNIE

units.text: Mags sets down the spoon.
She studies his hands, which are not quite steady.
A door opens at the rear.
A thin YOUNG LAWYER (20s, rain-soaked briefcase) slips in, looks from one to the other, and stops.
Mr. Delacorte, I told you not to speak without--
units.name: YOUNG LAWYER

units.text: Sit, Peter. The detective and I are only talking about ice cream.
units.name: VINNIE

units.text: Peter sits.
Mags stands, puts a card on the table, and tucks the spoon into her coat pocket.
Nobody leaves town.
units.name: MAGS

units.text: She goes out.
Vinnie stares at the cup she never touched, then slowly drinks it himself.
